measures.title: City of Davis Measure W (Willowgrove General Plan amendment)
measures.summary: Asks whether to adopt Resolution No. 26-052 amending the Davis General Plan to change the Willowgrove property, about 232 acres, from agricultural to urban land use designations and to set baseline project features. Per the City Attorney's impartial analysis, the project would allow 1,250 homes, including at least 250 deed-restricted affordable units, plus a community park, neighborhood retail and an agricultural buffer, and annexation of the site into the city could then proceed.
measures.yesMeans: The General Plan is amended to allow the Willowgrove development with its baseline project features.
measures.noMeans: The Willowgrove property keeps its agricultural designation.

measures.title: City of Woodland Sales Tax Measure
measures.summary: Asks whether Woodland should add a one-cent (1%) transactions and use (sales) tax, providing about $16 million a year, until ended by voters. Per the City Attorney's impartial analysis, it is a general tax that goes into the city's general fund for any lawful city purpose; the ballot question lists roads, police and fire protection, parks and trails, and public spaces.
measures.yesMeans: Woodland adds a one-cent sales tax with no end date.
measures.noMeans: The one-cent sales tax is not added.

measures.title: City of Woodland Measure (Urban Limit Line service extensions)
measures.summary: Amends the General Plan policy that voters adopted as Measure A in 2006, which bars the city from extending public services beyond its Urban Limit Line. The change would let the city extend sewer, water and recycled water service to existing commercial facilities on parcels within one mile of the line that were operating on or before November 3, 2026; it would not apply to new commercial or any residential development, and each extension would still need City Council approval.
measures.yesMeans: The city may extend sewer and water service to qualifying existing commercial properties near the Urban Limit Line.
measures.noMeans: The current ban on extending services beyond the Urban Limit Line stays as it is.
